entries.outcome: The parents' household (sheet 51, lines 40–45: Jean Baptiste 65, Claire 60, Jérémie 26, Célanire 22, a 'David' Gendron 13 and John Nadeau 5; image ark:/61903/3:1:S3HY-DZVQ-LDP) does not include Régis, and he is not on sheets 50–52, which were read directly. entries.name: Francois Regis GENDRON
entries.source: 11 November 2026 — Fur-trade records: HBCA biographical sheets, Saint-Boniface voyageur contracts, Red River census indexes
entries.outcome: No trace of Régis. The HBCA biographical index holds exactly one Gendron sheet — Alexandre (ca. 1811–1888/91) of St-Michel, Yamaska, in HBC service 1832–1853 in New Caledonia and at Fort Colville — a documented stranger. The Saint-Boniface voyageur contracts database ends in 1840, before Régis could have signed an engagement, so his absence there proves nothing. The only Gendron man in the Red River censuses is a François born about 1806–1809, resident there from 1838 — another stranger. The Montréal notarial route has since been searched: Généalogie Québec's notarial-contracts index holds no engagement for him, and the répertoires of the five Montréal engagement notaries whose practice reaches his era were read — Lacombe (name index, 1844–1863), Jobin (1844–1853) and Bédouin (1844) complete, and the chronological répertoires of Doucet (1844–1855) and Griffin (1844–1847) in full; no Gendron appears in any role, and none of the twenty engagements in Doucet's book names a Gendron or a Beauharnois man. One page of Griffin's répertoire (acts 20799–20837, October 1844) is missing from the scan. Correction, 12 November: HBCA DOES provide online name indexes for its engagement registers and servants' contracts. These indexes have now been checked; see the dated update below. Original engagement entries and annual accounts were subsequently inspected on 12 November; the separate contracts remain unread. See the original-record findings below.

entries.name: Francois Regis GENDRON

entries.outcome: Corrected the earlier assertion that no online engagement index exists. Gendron entries in both the Northern Department engagement index and the servants-contract index were examined. Four later François entries (1854, 1859, 1860, 1862) provide archival references but no identification as Régis, no parents, and no age in the displayed entries. At this initial index stage, the originals had not been read; subsequent original-record findings appear below.

entries.outcome: Baptism, daughter's baptism and burial re-read in the index. The only other Eusèbe Gendreau/Gendron of the generation (m.
